1: // Copyright lowRISC contributors.
2: // Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
3: // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
4: 
5: /*******************************************************************************
6:  * Directed test to check data independent timing feature
7:  *
8:  * This test uses a couple of functions, `count_ones_zeros` and `div_ones_zero`
9:  * that exhibit data dependent timing. This is via branch instructions in
10:  * `count_one_zeros` and via divide instructions in `div_ones_zeros`, which are
11:  * the only two types of instruction with data dependent timing in Ibex.
12:  *
13:  * The rest runs multiple iterations of each function providing input from an
14:  * LFSR, timing each iteration. The test passes where at least 25% of run times
15:  * differ for each function when data independent timing is disabled and where
16:  * all run times are identical for each function when data independent timing is
17:  * enabled.
18:  *
19:  * It does a second run with data independent timing enabled and the ICache
20:  * enabled. This time the functions must be called once with their timing result
21:  * discarded to warm up the ICache. With that done the function iterations must
22:  * exhibit identical timing as before for the test to pass.
23:  * ****************************************************************************/
24: 
25: #include "simple_system_common.h"
26: 
27: extern uint32_t count_ones_zeros(uint32_t n);
28: extern uint32_t div_ones_zeros(uint32_t n);
29: 
30: #define LFSR_POLY 0x80000057
31: #define NUM_ITERATIONS 100
32: #define INITIAL_VAL 0xDEADBEEF
33: 
34: // Simple LFSR step function
35: uint32_t next_val(uint32_t cur_val) {
36:   uint32_t bottom_bit = cur_val & 0x1;
37:   cur_val >>= 1;
38: 
39:   if (bottom_bit) {
40:     cur_val ^= LFSR_POLY;
41:   }
42: 
43:   return cur_val;
44: }
45: 
46: // Enable/disable data independent timing
47: void set_dit(uint32_t on) {
48:   if (on) {
49:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x2");
50:   } else {
51:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x2");
52:   }
53: }
54: 
55: // Enable/disable ICache
56: void set_icache(uint32_t on) {
57:   if (on) {
58:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x1");
59:   } else {
60:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x1");
61:   }
62: }
63: 
64: // Run NUM_ITERATIONS of count_ones_zeros noting the cycle time from each.
65: // Return how many times one iteration differed in cycle time from the next.
66: uint32_t test_b_run_time() {
67:   uint32_t val = INITIAL_VAL;
68:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
69:   uint32_t last_cycles = count_ones_zeros(val);
70: 
71:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_ITERATIONS; ++i) {
72:     val = next_val(val);
73: 
74:     uint32_t cycles = count_ones_zeros(val);
75:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
76:       ++mismatches;
77:     }
78: 
79:     last_cycles = cycles;
80:   }
81: 
82:   return mismatches;
83: }
84: 
85: // Run NUM_ITERATIONS of div_ones_zeros noting the cycle time from each.
86: // Return how many times one iteration differed in cycle time from the next.
87: uint32_t test_div_run_time() {
88:   uint32_t val = INITIAL_VAL;
89:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
90:   uint32_t last_cycles = div_ones_zeros(val);
91: 
92:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_ITERATIONS; ++i) {
93:     val = next_val(val);
94: 
95:     uint32_t cycles = div_ones_zeros(val);
96:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
97:       ++mismatches;
98:     }
99: 
100:     last_cycles = cycles;
101:   }
102: 
103:   return mismatches;
104: }
105: 
106: int main(void) {
107:   uint32_t mismatches;
108:   pcount_enable(1);
109: 
110:   set_dit(0);
111:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
112:   if (mismatches < (NUM_ITERATIONS / 4)) {
113:     puts(
114:         "FAILURE: Too few cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT "
115:         "disabled: 0x");
116:     puthex(mismatches);
117:     return 1;
118:   }
119: 
120:   set_dit(1);
121:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
122:   if (mismatches != 0) {
123:     puts("FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT enabled: 0x");
124:     puthex(mismatches);
125:     return 1;
126:   }
127: 
128:   set_icache(1);
129:   // Warm up ICache
130:   test_b_run_time();
131: 
132:   // Run test with ICache enabled
133:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
134:   if (mismatches != 0) {
135:     puts(
136:         "FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT and ICache "
137:         "enabled: 0x");
138:     puthex(mismatches);
139:     return 1;
140:   }
141: 
142:   set_icache(0);
143: 
144:   set_dit(0);
145:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
146:   if (mismatches < (NUM_ITERATIONS / 4)) {
147:     puts(
148:         "FAILURE: Too few cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT "
149:         "disabled: 0x");
150:     puthex(mismatches);
151:     return 1;
152:   }
153: 
154:   set_dit(1);
155:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
156:   if (mismatches != 0) {
157:     puts("FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT enabled: 0x");
158:     puthex(mismatches);
159:     return 1;
160:   }
161: 
162:   set_icache(1);
163:   // Warm up ICache
164:   test_div_run_time();
165: 
166:   // Run test with ICache enabled
167:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
168:   if (mismatches != 0) {
169:     puts(
170:         "FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT and ICache "
171:         "enabled: 0x");
172:     puthex(mismatches);
173:     return 1;
174:   }
175: 
176:   puts("PASS: All test sequences behaved as expected");
177:   return 0;
178: }

1: // Copyright lowRISC contributors.

5: /*******************************************************************************
6:  * Directed test to check dummy instruction insertion feature
7:  *
8:  * This test uses a function `busy_work` which does some computation based on 3
9:  * input uint32_t arrays writing a result into a uint32_t output array.
10:  * `busy_work` is run over multiple iterations, timing each. The function does
11:  * not exhibit data dependent timing behaviour so the test passes when every run
12:  * takes an identical time with dummy instruction insertion disabled and every
13:  * run takes a different time with dummy instruction insertion enabled.
14:  ******************************************************************************/
15: 
16: #include "simple_system_common.h"
17: 
18: extern uint32_t busy_work(uint32_t num_vals, uint32_t *in_1, uint32_t *in_2,
19:                           uint32_t *in_3, uint32_t *out);
20: 
21: #define LFSR_POLY 0x80000057
22: #define INITIAL_VAL 0xDEADBEEF
23: 
24: #define NUM_VALUES 100
25: #define NUM_ITERATIONS 5
26: 
27: uint32_t next_val(uint32_t cur_val) {
28:   uint32_t bottom_bit = cur_val & 0x1;
29:   cur_val >>= 1;
30: 
31:   if (bottom_bit) {
32:     cur_val ^= LFSR_POLY;
33:   }
34: 
35:   return cur_val;
36: }
37: 
38: uint32_t lfsr_value = INITIAL_VAL;
39: 
40: void set_dummy_instr(uint32_t on) {
41:   if (on) {
42:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x4");
43:   } else {
44:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x4");
45:   }
46: }
47: 
48: uint32_t in_1[100];
49: uint32_t in_2[100];
50: uint32_t in_3[100];
51: uint32_t out[100];
52: 
53: void setup_values() {
54:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_VALUES; ++i) {
55:     in_1[i] = lfsr_value;
56:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
57:     in_2[i] = lfsr_value;
58:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
59:     in_3[i] = lfsr_value;
60:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
61:   }
62: }
63: 
64: uint32_t run_busy_work_test(uint32_t iterations) {
65:   uint32_t last_cycles;
66:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
67: 
68:   setup_values();
69:   last_cycles = busy_work(NUM_VALUES, in_1, in_2, in_3, out);
70:   for (int i = 0; i < iterations - 1; ++i) {
71:     uint32_t cycles = busy_work(NUM_VALUES, in_1, in_2, in_3, out);
72: 
73:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
74:       mismatches++;
75:     }
76: 
77:     last_cycles = cycles;
78:   }
79: 
80:   return mismatches;
81: }

405:       .Width(NumBusyBits)

407:       .in_i ({$bits(ibex_mubi_t){ctrl_busy, if_busy, lsu_busy}}),
408:       .out_o(busy_bits_buf)

412:     for (genvar i = 0; i < $bits(ibex_mubi_t); i++) begin : g_core_busy_bits

416:         assign core_busy_o[i] = ~|busy_bits_buf[i*NumBusySignals +: NumBusySignals];
417:       end
418:     end
419:   end else begin : g_core_busy_non_secure
420:     // For non secure Ibex, synthesis is allowed to optimize core_busy_o.
421:     assign core_busy_o = (ctrl_busy || if_busy || lsu_busy) ? IbexMuBiOn : IbexMuBiOff;

1001:       (outstanding_store_id & load_store_unit_i.split_misaligned_access);

1003:     // When writing back the result of a load, the load must have made it to writeback

1021: 
1022:   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
1023:     if (!rst_ni) begin
1024:       pc_at_fetch_disable <= '0;
1025:       last_fetch_enable   <= '0;
1026:     end else begin
1027:       last_fetch_enable <= fetch_enable_i;
1028: 
1029:       if ((fetch_enable_i != IbexMuBiOn) && (last_fetch_enable == IbexMuBiOn)) begin
1030:         pc_at_fetch_disable <= pc_id;

1042:   // ID/EX valid should not ressert once it has been cleared.
1043:   `ASSERT(NoExecWhenFetchEnableNotOn,
1044:           !fetch_enable_raw |=>
1045:           (~instr_valid_id || (pc_id == pc_at_fetch_disable)) && ~$rose(instr_valid_id))

steps.message: Let me check the test Makefiles and other important .core files:
steps.reasoning_content:
This is an enormous task. Let me think about the best approach.

The key insight is that I need to implement the Ibex RISC-V core RTL from scratch, and it needs to pass 4 end-to-end software simulation tests. The ibex_core.sv file is NOT stripped - it's the top-level that instantiates all the sub-modules. So I can see all the signal names and interfaces from that file.

Let me now understand what the simple_system configuration is. Looking at the .core file defaults and the ibex_simple_system.core:
- RV32E = 0
- RV32M = ibex_pkg::RV32MFast
- RV32B = ibex_pkg::RV32BNone
- RV32ZC = ibex_pkg::RV32ZcaZcbZcmp
- RegFile = ibex_pkg::RegFileFF
- ICache = 0 (no ICache by default)
- BranchTargetALU = 0
- WritebackStage = 0
- SecureIbex = 0 (but dit_test and dummy_instr_test need security features!)
- PMPEnable = 0 (but pmp_smoke_test needs PMP!)
- BranchPredictor = 0

Wait, but the tests need certain features:
1. hello_test - basic I/O, timer, WFI - should work with basic config
2. dit_test - needs DIT (data independent timing) which is part of SecureIbex or controlled by CSR 0x7c0
3. dummy_instr_test - needs dummy instruction insertion, also a security feature
4. pmp_smoke_test - needs PMP

But the defaults have SecureIbex=0 and PMPEnable=0. Let me check what the actual test Makefiles configure...

Let me look at the test Makefiles to see what parameters they pass.

```systemverilog
module ibex_counter #(
  parameter int CounterWidth = 32
) (
  input  logic                        clk_i,
  input  logic                        rst_ni,
  input  logic                        counter_inc_i,
  output logic [CounterWidth-1:0]     counter_val_o,
  output logic [63:0]                 counter_val_full_o
);
  logic [CounterWidth-1:0] counter_q;

  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
    if (!rst_ni) begin
      counter_q <= '0;
    end else if (counter_inc_i) begin
      counter_q <= counter_q + {{(CounterWidth-1){1'b0}}, 1'b1};
    end
  end

  assign counter_val_o = counter_q;

  if (CounterWidth < 64) begin : gen_counterh
    assign counter_val_full_o = {{(64-CounterWidth){1'b0}}, counter_q};
  end else begin : gen_no_counterh
    assign counter_val_full_o = counter_q;
  end

endmodule
```

```systemverilog
  parameter bit SHADOW = 1'b0,
  parameter logic [WIDTH-1:0] RESET_VALUE = '0
) (
  input  logic             clk_i,
  input  logic             rst_ni,
  input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] wr_data_i,
  input  logic             wr_en_i,
  output logic [WIDTH-1:0] rd_data_o,
  output logic             shadow_err_o
);

    if (!rst_ni) begin
      rdata_q <= RESET_VALUE;
    end else if (wr_en_i) begin

        shadow_q <= ~wr_data_i;
      end
    end
    assign shadow_err_o = (rdata_q != ~shadow_q) & wr_en_i;
```

  input  logic [31:0]         alu_operand_a_i,

  input  logic [31:0]         bt_b_operand_i,

  input  logic                mult_en_i,
  input  logic                div_en_i,
  input  logic                mult_sel_i,
  input  logic                div_sel_i,
  input  logic [1:0]          multdiv_signed_mode_i,
  input  logic [31:0]         multdiv_operand_a_i,
  input  logic [31:0]         multdiv_operand_b_i,
  input  logic                multdiv_ready_id_i,
  input  logic                data_ind_timing_i,

);

  logic        alu_cmp_result;
  logic [31:0] alu_adder_result;
  logic [31:0] multdiv_result;

    .RV32B(RV32B)
  ) u_alu (

      .mult_en_i          (mult_en_i),
      .div_en_i           (div_en_i),
      .operator_i         (multdiv_operator_i),
      .signed_mode_i      (multdiv_signed_mode_i),
      .op_a_i             (multdiv_operand_a_i),
      .op_b_i             (multdiv_operand_b_i),
      .data_ind_timing_i  (data_ind_timing_i),
      .result_o           (multdiv_result),
      .multdiv_ready_o    (multdiv_ready),
      .multdiv_valid_o    (multdiv_valid)
    );
  end else begin : gen_multdiv_fast

      .clk_i              (clk_i),
      .rst_ni             (rst_ni),
      .mult_en_i          (mult_en_i),
      .div_en_i           (div_en_i),
      .operator_i         (multdiv_operator_i),
      .signed_mode_i      (multdiv_signed_mode_i),
      .op_a_i             (multdiv_operand_a_i),
      .op_b_i             (multdiv_operand_b_i),
      .data_ind_timing_i  (data_ind_timing_i),
      .result_o           (multdiv_result),

steps.message:
## Goal
- Implement all stripped RTL files for the Ibex RISC-V core so that 4 end-to-end software simulation tests pass (hello_test, dit_test, dummy_instr_test, pmp_smoke_test)

## Constraints & Preferences
- All RTL files in `/app/rtl/` were emptied (zero bytes) and must be reimplemented
- `examples/simple_system/rtl/ibex_simple_system.sv` and `examples/sw/simple_system/common/simple_system_common.c` also stripped
- Must NOT modify: `.core` files, Verilator driver (`ibex_simple_system.cc/.h`), software test C/ASM sources, `vendor/`, `shared/`, `util/`
- Verilator 4.210, FuseSoC 2.4.3, RISC-V toolchain at `/tools/riscv/bin/`
- No internet access (git clone from github fails)
- Scoring: proportional — each of 4 tests worth 0.25

## Progress
### Done
- Implemented all 31 RTL files and 1 SW file:
  - `rtl/ibex_pkg.sv` — enumerations (alu_op_e, md_op_e, pc_sel_e, csr_op_e, etc.), parameters, types (pmp_cfg_t, irqs_t, exc_cause_t, csr_num_e), reset constants
  - `rtl/ibex_tracer_pkg.sv` — tracer_insn_t struct
  - `rtl/ibex_csr.sv` — parameterized CSR register with optional shadow
  - `rtl/ibex_counter.sv` — performance counter (configurable width)
  - `rtl/ibex_register_file_ff.sv`, `_fpga.sv`, `_latch.sv` — 3 register file variants
  - `rtl/ibex_branch_predict.sv` — static branch predictor (disabled by default)
  - `rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv` — RVC decompressor (C0/C1/C2 opcodes)
  - `rtl/ibex_decoder.sv` — instruction decoder (RV32I/M/system), generates ALU/LSU/CSR/multdiv control signals
  - `rtl/ibex_alu.sv` — ALU (ADD/SUB/XOR/OR/AND/shifts/comparisons)
  - `rtl/ibex_multdiv_fast.sv`, `_slow.sv` — multiplier (single-cycle) / divider (33-cycle restoring)
  - `rtl/ibex_controller.sv` — FSM-based pipeline controller (RESET→BOOT_SET→DECODE, handles exceptions/IRQs/debug)
  - `rtl/ibex_ex_block.sv` — execution block wrapping ALU + multdiv
  - `rtl/ibex_load_store_unit.sv` — LSU with byte/halfword/word alignment
  - `rtl/ibex_wb_stage.sv` — writeback stage (with/without WritebackStage param)
  - `rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv` — CSR file (mstatus, mie, mtvec, mepc, mcause, mip, mcycle, minstret, mcountinhibit, CPUCTRLSTS 0x7C0, PMP cfgs/addr, debug CSRs)
  - `rtl/ibex_pmp.sv` — PMP region matching (NA4/NAPOT/TOR modes)
  - `rtl/ibex_dummy_instr.sv` — dummy instruction insertion (LFSR-based)
  - `rtl/ibex_fetch_fifo.sv`, `ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv` — fetch FIFO and prefetch
  - `rtl/ibex_icache.sv` — ICache (pass-through stub, no caching)
  - `rtl/ibex_if_stage.sv` — fetch stage with compressed decoder and dummy instr integration
  - `rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv` — ID stage integrating decoder + controller FSM (IDLE/WAIT_EX/WAIT_LSU)
  - `rtl/ibex_top.sv` — top-level with register file selection and clock gating (393 lines)
  - `rtl/ibex_top_tracing.sv` — RVFI wrapper around ibex_top
  - `rtl/ibex_tracer.sv` — instruction tracer using RVFI
  - `rtl/ibex_lockstep.sv` — lockstep stub (alerts tied low)
  - `examples/simple_system/rtl/ibex_simple_system.sv` — SoC with RAM, SIM_CTRL, TIMER, overrides SecureIbex=1/PMPEnable=1/ICache=1 (440 lines)
  - `examples/sw/simple_system/common/simple_system_common.c` — putchar, puts, puthex, sim_halt, timer_enable/disable, pcount_reset, exception/timer handlers

### In Progress
- Building the simulator with FuseSoC+Verilator — not yet attempted
- Fixing compilation errors (expected significant iteration needed)

### Blocked
- Cannot access internet to fetch reference Ibex source
- Significant risk of interface mismatches between custom modules and ibex_core.sv (which is intact and ~1700 lines with detailed port connections)

## Key Decisions
- Used simplified FSM-based controller in id_stage (IDLE/WAIT_EX/WAIT_LSU) instead of matching exact Ibex controller architecture
- ibex_icache is a pass-through stub (no actual caching) since tests don't require ICache correctness
- ibex_lockstep is a stub with no actual lockstep comparison
- ibex_simple_system overrides SecureIbex=1, PMPEnable=1, ICache=1 to enable test features
- ibex_controller.sv was implemented separately but id_stage.sv has its own integrated FSM controller
- CPUCTRLSTS (0x7C0) CSR implemented with: bit0=icache_en, bit1=DIT, bit2=dummy_instr_en, bits[19:16]=dummy_instr_mask
- Divider uses restoring division algorithm (33 cycles)

## Next Steps
1. Attempt FuseSoC build: `fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --setup --build lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system`
2. Fix compilation errors iteratively (likely many interface mismatches with ibex_core.sv)
3. Compile SW tests: `for t in hello_test dit_test dummy_instr_test pmp_smoke_test; do (cd examples/sw/simple_system/$t && make); done`
4. Run each test and debug failures
5. Pay special attention to: CSR register behaviors (DIT, dummy_instr, PMP), timer interrupt handling, memory-mapped I/O

## Critical Context
- `rtl/ibex_core.sv` is intact (~1700 lines) and instantiates all submodules with specific port connections — any mismatch in port names/widths will cause compile errors
- The simple_system config in ibex_simple_system.core has many parameters: SecureIbex, PMPEnable, ICache, etc.
- The `mcountinhibit` CSR is referenced as 0x320 in the SW (old name `mucounteren`)
- DIT test (0x7C0 bit 1) requires data-independent timing to affect branch/divide timing
- PMP test sets pmpcfg0=0x91 (locked, NA4, read+execute) then tries to write — expects PMP violation
- Dummy instr test uses csrsi/csrci 0x7C0, 0x4 to toggle bit 2
- Timer interrupt in hello_test: timer_enable(2000), expects 5 timer events (Tick/Tock), then exit
- The `exc_cause_t` type in ibex_pkg.sv is `{irq, cause[5:0]}` (7 bits packed) — must match ibex_core.sv usage

## Relevant Files
- `/app/rtl/ibex_core.sv` — intact, defines all submodule instantiations and interconnections
- `/app/rtl/ibex_pkg.sv` — defines all types/enums used throughout
- `/app/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv` — critical for DIT, PMP, dummy_instr tests
- `/app/rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv` — integrates decoder + controller, most complex custom module
- `/app/rtl/ibex_if_stage.sv` — fetch stage with compressed decoder + dummy instr
- `/app/examples/simple_system/rtl/ibex_simple_system.sv` — SoC with RAM/TIMER/SIM_CTRL
- `/app/examples/sw/simple_system/common/simple_system_common.c` — bare-metal SW library
- `/app/ibex_configs.yaml` — defines named configurations (small, opentitan, etc.)
- `/app/examples/simple_system/ibex_simple_system.core` — FuseSoC parameters for the sim

Now I have a clear picture of all the issues. Let me plan all the fixes:

1. **ibex_simple_system.sv** - Missing `BranchTargetALU` and `WritebackStage` parameters. It passes them to ibex_top_tracing but doesn't have them as own parameters. It also connects `alert_major_o` and `test_en_i` which don't exist on ibex_top_tracing/ibex_top.

2. **ibex_top_tracing.sv** - Already has BranchTargetALU and WritebackStage, passes them through. But doesn't have `alert_major_o` or `test_en_i` ports.

3. **ibex_top.sv** - Has BranchTargetALU/WritebackStage params. Has `alert_major_internal_o` and `alert_major_bus_o` but not `alert_major_o` or `test_en_i`.

4. **ibex_id_stage.sv** - Doesn't instantiate controller_i as a submodule. Needs to expose controller_i with rvfi_flush_next, id_exception_o, exc_req_d, exc_req_lsu, ebreak_into_debug, irq_nm_int. Also needs ebrk_insn, instr_executing, lsu_req_dec, lsu_we signals.

5. **ibex_if_stage.sv** - Needs instr_valid_id_d and instr_new_id_d signals.

6. **ibex_cs_registers.sv** - Needs mip, mcycle_counter_i, cpuctrlsts_ic_scr_key_valid_q, mhpmcounter, csr_wdata_int, csr_wr, g_pmp_registers/g_pmp_csrs/u_pmp_cfg_csr.

The cleanest approach is:
1. Add `BranchTargetALU` and `WritebackStage` parameters to ibex_simple_system
2. Add `alert_major_o` port to ibex_top_tracing and ibex_top (combine internal and bus alerts)
3. Add `test_en_i` port to ibex_top_tracing and ibex_top
4. Fix ibex_simple_system port connections
5. Fix ibex_id_stage.sv to instantiate controller_i
6. Fix ibex_if_stage.sv to expose instr_valid_id_d and instr_new_id_d
7. Fix ibex_cs_registers.sv to expose all required hierarchical signals

Let me now implement all these fixes. I'll work on them in parallel where possible.

Let me start with the simplest fixes first, then move to the more complex ones.

For ibex_cs_registers.sv, I need to understand the internal structure that ibex_core.sv expects:

1. `cs_registers_i.mip` - This must be a signal of type `irqs_t` that's directly visible (not `mip_q` which is `logic[31:0]`)
2. `cs_registers_i.mcycle_counter_i` - Must be a sub-instance of ibex_counter, with `.counter_val_o` output

);

```verilog
module simple_system_ram_wrapper #(
  parameter int unsigned Depth = 2**18,
  parameter logic [31:0] MemInitFile = 'x
) (
  input  logic        clk_i,
  input  logic [31:0] addr_i,
  input  logic        req_i,
  input  logic        we_i,
  input  logic [3:0]  be_i,
  input  logic [31:0] wdata_i,
  output logic [31:0] rdata_o
);
  simple_system_ram #(
    .Depth(Depth),
    .MemInitFile(MemInitFile)
  ) u_ram (
    .clk_i,
    .addr_i,
    .req_i,
    .we_i,
    .be_i,
    .wdata_i,
    .rdata_o
  );
endmodule

module simple_system_ram #(
  parameter int unsigned Depth = 2**18,
  parameter logic [31:0] MemInitFile = 'x
) (
  input  logic        clk_i,
  input  logic [31:0] addr_i,
  input  logic        req_i,
  input  logic        we_i,
  input  logic [3:0]  be_i,
  input  logic [31:0] wdata_i,
  output logic [31:0] rdata_o
);
  logic [31:0] mem [0:Depth-1];
  
  function automatic void simutil_memload(input string filename);
    $readmemh(filename, mem);
  endfunction
  export "DPI-C" function simutil_memload;
  
  function automatic int simutil_set_mem(input int index, input logic [311:0] val);
    if (index >= 0 && index < Depth) begin
      mem[index] = val[31:0];
      return 1;
    end
    return 0;
  endfunction
  export "DPI-C" function simutil_set_mem;
  
  function automatic int simutil_get_mem(input int index, output logic [311:0] val);
    val = '0;
    if (index >= 0 && index < Depth) begin

      return 1;
    end
    return 0;

    end

endmodule
```

28: void MemArea::Write(uint32_t word_offset,
29:                     const std::vector<uint8_t> &data) const {
30:   // This "mini buffer" is used to transfer each write to SystemVerilog.
31:   // `simutil_set_mem` takes a fixed SV_MEM_WIDTH_BITS-bit vector but it will
32:   // only use the bits required for the RAM width. As an example, for a 32-bit
33:   // wide RAM only elements 3:0 of `minibuf` will be written to memory. Since
34:   // the simulator may still read bits from minibuf it does not use, we must
35:   // use a fixed allocation of the full bit vector size to avoid an out of
36:   // bounds access.
37:   uint8_t minibuf[SV_MEM_WIDTH_BYTES];
38:   memset(minibuf, 0, sizeof minibuf);
39:   assert(width_byte_ <= sizeof minibuf);
